title: Give the first 90 work minutes to creation, not communication.
subtitle: First-block boundary
rationale: Spend the day's freshest attention on the hardest work before the inbox sets the agenda.

evidence.summary: A widely adopted practitioner pattern consistent with interruption research; the specific first-block design is untested in trials.

indications: Workdays open with email, chat, or news by default.
The most important project advances only on meeting-free days.
Mornings are reliably the highest-energy hours.
